feat(torch_ops): in-place e4m3fn→e4m3fnuz conversion + fnuz-storage decode variants (#71)

The grouped native-fp8 path's copy-based conversion cache doubled
expert-weight residency (~9.7 GiB/layer permanent) and its ~19 GiB fp32
transient OOM-swallowed conversions under a fixed HBM floor.

The fnuz remap is a pure per-byte function, so e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace
rewrites the checkpoint bytes IN PLACE through a 256-entry LUT:

- converted stack shares the checkpoint storage (no second resident copy)
- no fp32 materialization — peak extra memory is chunk-sized
  (chunk_bytes, default 1 GiB), so every layer can group
- scales are doubled in place (halving is exact: for every finite e4m3fn
  value v, fnuz_encode(v/2) · 2s == fn_encode(v) · s bitwise; fn NaN
  0x7f/0xff -> fnuz NaN 0x80; -0 -> +0)
- caller keeps the parameter buffers (floe's invalidation contract)

Consumers decode fnuz storage via expert_gemv / gather_dequant with
storage="e4m3fnuz": the launch passes an IS_FNUZ constexpr to the manual
decode (native bitcast is only valid for fn), value·scale identical to
the fn path. CUDA fn path still uses the zero-cost native cast.

Storage stays labeled e4m3fn on the rewritten buffers (floe's reload
path copies e4m3fn checkpoint bytes into them); the fnuz interpretation
is carried by the storage kwarg, and floe tracks conversion state with
the (data_ptr, _version, device) marker pattern from #69.

Tests: exhaustive 256-byte LUT vs the cast reference, value-exactness of
the halving map, storage-sharing, chunked-vs-single-shot, guards, plus
GPU-gated on-device conversion parity and bit-exact GEMV / gather /
grouped-native equivalence on the converted stacks.
